title: Replying to @JeffreyS✦theatre+trivia+travel At least I didn’t spoil t...
transcript: Alright, let's talk about spoilers in TikTok Theatre reviews, because this leads to another conversation I've actually been thinking a lot about recently. And to be honest, you're not the first person to accuse me of this, so you know, I'm open to that feedback. I'm still trying to find that line, but I have a few thoughts in response. First of all, with the Holes specifically, there's a lot more to that play than what I revealed in the opening line of my video. Not only more reveals that I didn't spoil, but more to take away from the viewing experience that has nothing to do with the mystery. And to be clear, I've never given away like the big ending spoiler of a play, but something that happens maybe 30 to 40 minutes into a 2 hour play, maybe. Especially when it's an important component of knowing what you're in for and being able to discuss the play and frankly, when it's the most interesting way in for people who haven't heard of it. You know, positioning something in a way that will do well on the algorithm is obviously a game we're all trying to play here. And in the case of the Holes, unfortunately, not to brag, but it did work pretty well. And there's a self serving component to that. Obviously I want people to watch my videos, but I also genuinely want more people to know about these plays, which leads me to the larger conversation I've been thinking about recently, which is that I think a lot of theater marketing right now is being a little too withholding. It's almost a stylistic thing. I think *they* think they're being coy and mysterious, but so many times recently I've walked into a play and been like, “wait, oh, actually, it turns out I didn't know what this was about.” And like, not to wade into the Midnight drama. I wasn't planning to comment on this, except that it does relate to this conversation right now. One of the big components of that drama was that they didn't use the word “slave” or “slavery” and people were going in not knowing that that was the subject matter. I also reviewed a show recently where the playwright reposted the review with a spoiler warning and I was genuinely shocked. I was like, *this* is the one I'm getting called out on? Like, the Holes I actually get. Like, I disagree, obviously, for the reasons I mentioned, but like, it's a fair note. I understand. This other one, I was like, genuinely, what are you talking about? Nothing in here is a spoiler. I fear that we might have lost the plot. Literally. Like, at a certain point, do you not want (A) more people to know your show exists? And (B) do we not wanna use operative words that will tangibly increase people's interest in the show? Again, there is a Self serving side of this, I'm not denying that, but both things are true. This over correction on withholding information is something that has genuinely frustrated me as an audience member. But like I said, it's blurry. It's case by case. So rest assured, it's something I'm thinking about and figuring out how to navigate in real time. So I appreciate the feedback.
